result.title: In-Context Learning for System Identification: Probabilistic Formulation, Long-Sequence Handling, and Benchmark Validation
result.summary: Traditional system identification typically involves two steps: initially, training data is processed to estimate a model of the system of interest; then, the model is used to predict outputs for new input queries. In contrast, recent in-context learning approaches learn a meta model that maps directly from training data and query inputs to outputs in a zero-shot fashion, bypassing explicit model estimation. This approach leverages a meta model trained offline, on large sets of synthetically generated data, to emulate the behavior of a system identification algorithm. In this work, we advance this meta-learning framework for system identification in three directions. First, we develop a unified probabilistic meta-identification architecture that combines a Transformer-based encoder-decoder with tailored mechanisms for handling long training sequences, enabling calibrated predictions over long horizons. Second, we show how a pre-trained meta model can act as an uncertainty-aware synthetic data generator for classical system identification, providing task-specific data that regularize parametric models when real data are scarce. Third, we systematically evaluate the framework on standard nonlinear system identification benchmarks and on a challenging out-of-distribution scenario, demonstrating competitive accuracy with state-of-the-art methods and strong generalization, including cases where input-only adaptation is sufficient to handle significant distribution shifts.

AI.brief_summary: 面向系统辨识的 in-context 元学习框架：提出结合 Transformer 编码器-解码器与长训练序列处理机制的概率化元辨识架构，并让预训练元模型充当不确定性感知的合成数据生成器，在非线性基准与分布外场景上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作不含视觉输入、不研究 VLM 推理，但其长上下文序列处理与概率化校准预测机制，可能为 LVR 的长度泛化、长序列上下文利用与不确定性驱动的证据筛选/停止决策提供可核查的方法线索。
